faqs.a: The calculator takes the reference date minus your birth date, counting whole calendar years first, then whole months, then the leftover days. From 1 January 2000 to 18 October 2026 that gives 26 years, 9 months and 17 days.
faqs.q: How is age in years, months and days calculated?

faqs.a: Months have 28 to 31 days, so borrowing days across a month boundary can look surprising — for example 31 January to 30 March shows as 1 month and 27 days. The total-days number is always exact, so trust that for precise durations.
faqs.q: Why does the result look odd around month ends?

faqs.a: In non-leap years your birthday is counted on 28 February and the next-birthday countdown points there. In leap years it lands on 29 February itself.
faqs.q: I was born on 29 February. How is my birthday handled?

faqs.a: Yes. Change the 'Age at date' field to any date on or after your birth date, and every screen — age, totals, next birthday — is recalculated for that day.
faqs.q: Can I find my age on a date in the past?

faqs.a: No. The page runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded, saved or shared.
faqs.q: Is my date of birth stored anywhere?

faqs.a: Days, weeks, hours and minutes are exact, counted from midnight on your birth date. Seconds tick live from the moment you open the page. Heartbeats and breaths are estimates from average rates of 70 per minute and 16 per minute.
faqs.q: How accurate are the lifetime totals?

age-calculator.formula: Age = reference date minus date of birth, counted as whole calendar years first, then whole months, then the remaining days. Totals build on the exact day count: weeks = days / 7, hours = days x 24, minutes = hours x 60.
howTo: Pick your date of birth in the first field.
Optionally change 'Age at date' to find your age on a specific past or present day.
Read your exact age on the Main screen.
Use the tabs to explore totals, your next birthday, birth details and fun stats.
keyFacts: Your age is counted from your date of birth up to today, or up to a date you choose.
Leap years are handled automatically — 29 February birthdays work in every year.
Calendar months have different lengths, so one 'month' of age is not a fixed number of days.
The seconds counter ticks live while this page stays open.
Heartbeat and breath totals are rough estimates from average rates, not medical measurements.
limitations: Month-end quirk: from 31 January to 30 March the tool reports 1 month and 27 days, because it borrows February's 28 days. Calendar months are irregular by nature.
The total-days figure is always exact — use it when you need a precise duration.
Dates before 1 January 1900 are not accepted.
Heartbeat and breath figures assume fixed average rates and are illustrative only.

age-calculator.workedExample: Born 1 January 2000, measured on 18 October 2026: years = 2026 - 2000 = 26; months = 10 - 1 = 9; days = 18 - 1 = 17. Result: 26 years, 9 months, 17 days — a total of 9,787 days, which is 321 months or 1,398 weeks.
